content:
**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Fallen/lodged corn plant with dead tan-brown leaves
- Stalk shows clear dark purplish-brown to black discoloration on the outer rind
- The blackening appears to spread along the stalk rind, not just at a single node
- Plant has collapsed/lodged

**Candidate narrowing:**
- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Shiny black rind discoloration, dark water-soaked lesions coalescing into black blotches/streaks, lodging — matches well
- **Physoderma stalk rot**: Black at specific nodes only, plants snap at node — less consistent (test image shows broader rind blackening, not just a node)
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: White mold, small black pycnidia — no mold visible

**Reference comparison:**
- Anthracnose stalk rot reference shows the same pattern: fallen/lodged plant with dark brownish-black rind discoloration extending along the stalk, matching the test image's stalk coloring and plant posture closely
- Physoderma stalk rot reference shows localized black node areas — doesn't match the broader rind darkening seen here

The dark shiny-black rind discoloration spreading along the stalk combined with lodging is the hallmark of Anthracnose stalk rot.
